title: Chemical equilibrium 1: reversible, Q and K - 123 school
heading: Chemical equilibrium 1: reversible, Q and K
intro: Choose the correct answer for each question. Use a calculator where needed.

questions.question: What does the sign ⇌ in a reaction equation mean?
What holds in a chemical equilibrium for the forward and reverse reaction?

answers.a: only the reverse reaction goes on
answers.c: only the forward reaction goes on

questions.question: What is true about the concentrations at equilibrium?
What is a condition for an equilibrium to arise?

answers.a: an excess of a starting substance

questions.question: What is the equilibrium condition of N<sub>2</sub> + 3 H<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2 NH<sub>3</sub>?
What is the equilibrium condition of H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2 HI?
What is the equilibrium condition of 2 NO<sub>2</sub> ⇌ N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub>?
What is the equilibrium condition of CaCO<sub>3</sub> (s) ⇌ CaO (s) + CO<sub>2</sub> (g)?
What is the equilibrium condition of C (s) + CO<sub>2</sub> (g) ⇌ 2 CO (g)?
Which substances do not appear in the equilibrium condition?
What is the concentration quotient Q?

answers.a: the fraction of K with the concentrations at any moment
answers.b: the value of K at 298 K
answers.c: the fraction of K with only the initial concentrations
answers.d: the difference between forward and reverse reaction

questions.question: What holds at equilibrium?
Q is smaller than K. What happens?

answers.a: the reaction goes to the right overall
answers.c: the reaction goes to the left overall

questions.question: Q is greater than K. What happens?

answers.a: the reaction goes to the right overall
answers.b: the reaction goes to the left overall

questions.question: What does K depend on?

answers.a: on the reaction and the temperature
answers.b: on the volume of the vessel

questions.question: What does a catalyst do to K?
A reaction has a very large K. What does that mean?

answers.c: at equilibrium there are mainly reaction products
answers.d: at equilibrium there are mainly starting substances

questions.question: A reaction has a very small K. What does that mean?

answers.b: at equilibrium there are mainly reaction products
answers.d: at equilibrium there are mainly starting substances

questions.question: For H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2 HI at equilibrium [H<sub>2</sub>] = 0.10, [I<sub>2</sub>] = 0.10 and [HI] = 0.40 mol/L. What is K?
For 2 SO<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2 SO<sub>3</sub> at equilibrium [SO<sub>2</sub>] = 0.20, [O<sub>2</sub>] = 0.10 and [SO<sub>3</sub>] = 0.40 mol/L. What is K?
Assume that for N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> ⇌ 2 NO<sub>2</sub> K = 0.20. Now [N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub>] = 0.50 and [NO<sub>2</sub>] = 0.10 mol/L. What is Q and what happens?

answers.b: Q = 2.0; the reaction goes to the left
answers.c: Q = 0.020; the reaction goes to the left
answers.d: Q = 0.020; the reaction goes to the right

questions.question: For A + B ⇌ C, K = 4.0. At equilibrium [A] = 0.20 and [B] = 0.50 mol/L. What is [C]?
For H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2 HI, K = 50. At equilibrium [H<sub>2</sub>] = [I<sub>2</sub>] = 0.10 mol/L. What is [HI]?
For H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2 HI at equilibrium [H<sub>2</sub>] = 0.20, [I<sub>2</sub>] = 0.20 and [HI] = 1.60 mol/L. What is K?
